correctness.rationale: For a same-part outside pair, every selected vertex has equal distances to the pair; for a cross-part outside pair, a selected vertex is equidistant exactly when it lies in a third part. This proves the iff characterization by a complete case split on whether some part is fully selected and on the number of supported parts. Invalid sets then decompose disjointly into support sizes zero, one, and two with nonempty proper part-subsets, giving the multivariate and univariate enumerators. The minimum-set classification follows from the same criterion. Exhaustive direct-definition verification covers all 8084 subsets of all 58 complete multipartite isomorphism types through order eight and matches every coefficient vector and minimum-count prediction.

originality.rationale: The original 2021 equidistant-dimension paper was checked and its complete-multipartite minimum formulas are treated as prior work. A 2024 complexity/lexicographic-product follow-up and current related equidistant-dimension literature were checked for stronger or equivalent coverage. Acceptance-time semantic searches using the exact structural criterion, generating-polynomial form, parameter synonyms, and minimum-set enumeration found no equivalent result; the closest published-result records concern different complete-multipartite parameters. The accumulated local ledger contains no equidistant or distance-equalizer finding. The novelty claim is restricted to the all-set structural characterization and its enumerative consequences.

value.rationale: The theorem upgrades a single extremal number to a complete feasible-set classification. It yields exact selection-profile counts, a multivariate enumerator retaining part information, the ordinary size polynomial, total counts, and exact minimum-basis counts for every complete multipartite graph. These are reusable structural data for probabilistic, weighted, and comparative questions, not a routine increment of the known dimension formula.
